questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The central Right to Information Act that applies to Jammu & Kashmir today was enacted by Parliament in which year?
questions.explanation: Parliament enacted the central RTI Act in 2005, and it became applicable to J&K only on 31 October 2019, when the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 came into force. '2009' is the commonest trap — that is the year of the erstwhile J&K Right to Information Act, 2009, J&K's own law, which the Reorganisation Act repealed. '2007' and '2003' correspond to no RTI enactment at either the central or the J&K level.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the RTI Act, 2005 as it applies to Jammu & Kashmir:

(i) It gives citizens the right to access information held by public authorities.
(ii) At the national level it replaced the Freedom of Information Act, 2002.
(iii) Since 31 October 2019 it extends to the Union Territories of J&K and Ladakh.
(iv) It applies directly to private companies and private individuals.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Act creates a citizen's right of access to information held by public authorities. (ii) is correct — it superseded the weaker Freedom of Information Act, 2002. (iii) is correct — the central Act reached J&K and Ladakh on 31 October 2019 under the Reorganisation Act, which simultaneously repealed the J&K RTI Act, 2009. (iv) is wrong — the Act binds public authorities, not private companies or individuals, though information about a private body that a public authority can lawfully access may be obtained through it.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: An applicant in Anantnag files an RTI application with a J&K UT public authority. Within how many days must the information ordinarily be supplied?
questions.explanation: Section 7 requires the Public Information Officer to decide within 30 days of receiving the request, and this is the timeline that has applied in J&K since the central Act was extended there in 2019. '15 days' is wrong — no such general limit exists, though a request routed through an Assistant PIO gets five extra days. '45 days' is wrong — 45 days applies in no ordinary case. '60 days' is wrong — that exceeds every limit in the Act; the only shorter special timeline is 48 hours where life or liberty is involved.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Extending the central RTI Act, 2005 to Jammu & Kashmir in 2019 was expected to strengthen transparency in the Union Territory's administration.
Reason (R): An informed citizenry is essential for a functioning democracy to hold the government accountable.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — the central Act replaced the repealed J&K RTI Act, 2009 from 31 October 2019 and brought J&K public authorities within the central transparency regime, including appeals to the Central Information Commission. (R) is correct — the Act's own preamble rests on the premise that an informed citizenry is vital to democracy and to containing corruption. (R) is also the explanation of (A): it states exactly why extending the Act was expected to improve accountability, so the options denying the causal link or rejecting either statement are wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are among the Section 8 exemptions that a Public Information Officer in J&K UT may invoke to refuse an RTI request?

(i) Information that would affect the sovereignty and integrity of India
(ii) Information relating to cabinet papers including records of deliberations
(iii) Information that would endanger the life or physical safety of any person
(iv) Information about the salaries of government employees

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i), (ii) and (iii) are all express exemptions under Section 8 — sovereignty and integrity of India, cabinet papers while a decision is pending, and information endangering someone's life or physical safety. Given J&K's security situation, the first and third are invoked comparatively often there. (iv) is wrong — the pay of government employees is routinely held to be disclosable public information and is in fact part of the proactive disclosure expected under Section 4, so any option containing (iv) must be rejected.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: For an RTI application to a public authority in J&K UT under the central Act, the prescribed application fee is:
questions.explanation: The prescribed fee for an RTI application to a central public authority is Rs. 10, and this is the fee that applies in J&K UT since the central Act was extended in 2019. Applicants below the poverty line pay nothing. 'Rs. 100' is wrong — that is far above the prescribed rate and would defeat the Act's accessibility. 'Rs. 50' is wrong — no such fee is prescribed. 'Rs. 5' is wrong — it understates the standard fee, which has remained Rs. 10.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following authorities under the RTI regime with their roles in Jammu & Kashmir:

Column I:
(a) Public Information Officer (PIO)
(b) First Appellate Authority
(c) Central Information Commission (CIC)
(d) J&K State Information Commission

Column II:
(i) Hears second appeals from J&K UT public authorities today
(ii) Receives RTI applications and furnishes the information
(iii) Hears the first appeal against a PIO's decision
(iv) Heard second appeals in J&K until it was wound up after 2019

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The PIO is the officer who receives applications and supplies information, so (a)-(ii). The First Appellate Authority, an officer senior to the PIO within the same public authority, hears the first appeal, so (b)-(iii). Since the central Act was extended to J&K in 2019, second appeals from J&K public authorities lie to the Central Information Commission, so (c)-(i). The J&K State Information Commission, created under the repealed J&K RTI Act, 2009, ceased to function after reorganisation, so (d)-(iv). Every other option misplaces at least two of these roles.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: If a Public Information Officer of a J&K UT public authority fails to furnish information within the prescribed time, the penalty the Information Commission may impose is:
options: Rs. 500 per day up to maximum Rs. 50,000
Rs. 250 per day up to maximum Rs. 25,000
Rs. 100 per day up to maximum Rs. 10,000
Rs. 1000 per day up to maximum Rs. 1,00,000
questions.correctAnswer: Rs. 250 per day up to maximum Rs. 25,000
questions.explanation: Section 20 empowers the Information Commission to impose a penalty of Rs. 250 for each day of delay, subject to a ceiling of Rs. 25,000, and since 2019 that power over J&K public authorities rests with the Central Information Commission. 'Rs. 500 per day up to Rs. 50,000' doubles both figures. 'Rs. 100 per day up to Rs. 10,000' understates both. 'Rs. 1000 per day up to Rs. 1,00,000' is far beyond anything the section permits. Note the penalty falls personally on the PIO, not on the department.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Central Information Commission, which now hears second appeals from Jammu & Kashmir:

(i) It consists of a Chief Information Commissioner and up to ten Information Commissioners.
(ii) Members are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee headed by the Prime Minister.
(iii) It hears second appeals against the decisions of First Appellate Authorities.
(iv) The Central Information Commission is located in Mumbai.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Commission comprises the Chief Information Commissioner and not more than ten Information Commissioners. (ii) is correct — they are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee chaired by the Prime Minister. (iii) is correct — it is the second-appellate forum, and since 2019 J&K appeals come to it rather than to the wound-up J&K State Information Commission. (iv) is wrong — the Commission sits in New Delhi, not Mumbai, so every option containing (iv) fails. Note that the RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019 shifted the tenure and service conditions of Commissioners to rules made by the Central Government.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: An applicant in Srinagar seeks information concerning the life or liberty of a person. Under the RTI Act such information must be provided within:
questions.explanation: Section 7(1) requires information concerning the life or liberty of a person to be supplied within 48 hours of the request, the shortest timeline in the Act, against the ordinary 30 days. '7 days' is wrong — no such period appears in the Act. '24 hours' is wrong — it is shorter than the statute allows and a common misremembering. '15 days' is wrong — that is neither the ordinary limit of 30 days nor the special 48-hour limit; the only place five extra days arise is where an application is routed through an Assistant PIO.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A Below Poverty Line applicant in Kupwara is exempt from paying the RTI application fee.
Reason (R): The RTI Act aims to ensure that even economically weaker sections can access information without financial barriers.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — applicants certified as below the poverty line pay no application fee and no fee for copies, and this applies to J&K UT under the central Act extended in 2019. (R) is correct — the exemption exists precisely so that cost does not shut the poor out of the transparency regime. (R) is therefore the correct explanation of (A). The option denying the causal link is wrong because the waiver flows directly from that objective, and the two options rejecting either statement are wrong because both are accurate.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Section 24 of the RTI Act, read with the Second Schedule, excludes certain central intelligence and security organisations, an exclusion that applies to RTI requests in J&K UT as well. Which of the following are so excluded?

(i) Intelligence Bureau (IB)
(ii) Research and Analysis Wing (RAW)
(iii) Election Commission of India
(iv) National Technical Research Organisation (NTRO)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The Second Schedule lists central intelligence and security organisations placed outside the Act by Section 24, and the Intelligence Bureau (i), the Research and Analysis Wing (ii) and the National Technical Research Organisation (iv) are all on it. (iii) is wrong — the Election Commission of India is a constitutional body and an ordinary public authority for RTI purposes, fully answerable under the Act. Every option containing (iii), including 'All of the above', is therefore incorrect. Note that even for listed bodies, information on allegations of corruption and human rights violations is not shielded.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: An applicant in Jammu is dissatisfied with a PIO's reply. The first appeal must be filed within how many days of receiving the response, or of the date the response was due?
questions.explanation: Section 19(1) allows a first appeal within 30 days of the PIO's decision or of the expiry of the period within which the decision should have been given, and this is the timeline in J&K UT under the central Act. '60 days' is wrong — that is the window for the second appeal to the Information Commission, a distinction candidates frequently confuse. '15 days' is wrong — no such appeal period exists. '45 days' is wrong — it matches neither the first nor the second appeal period.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Section 4 of the RTI Act and its application to J&K UT departments:

(i) It mandates proactive (suo motu) disclosure of information by public authorities.
(ii) Public authorities must publish information about their organisation, functions and duties.
(iii) They must publish details of their budget, subsidy programmes and beneficiaries.
(iv) Proactive disclosure reduces the need for individual RTI applications for that information.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All four are correct. (i) Section 4 obliges every public authority to disclose specified categories on its own initiative, without waiting for a request. (ii) and (iii) are among the enumerated heads — organisation, functions and duties, and budget, subsidy programmes and their beneficiaries — and J&K UT departments have been bound by them since the central Act was extended in 2019. (iv) follows logically, since the Act's stated aim is that citizens should need to file as few applications as possible. Each of the other options omits at least one correct statement.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The central RTI Act, 2005, the law now in force in J&K UT, contains how many sections in total?
questions.explanation: The RTI Act, 2005 is a compact statute of 31 sections arranged in six chapters, together with two Schedules, and it is this Act that has governed J&K since 31 October 2019. '21 sections' understates the count. '25 sections' is likewise short of the correct figure. '35 sections' overstates it. A useful anchor is that the operative provisions candidates are asked about — Section 4 proactive disclosure, Section 6 requests, Section 8 exemptions, Section 19 appeals, Section 20 penalties and Section 24 exclusions — all fall inside those 31 sections.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Who may file an RTI application with a public authority in Jammu & Kashmir UT?
questions.explanation: The right belongs to every citizen of India, and since the central Act was extended to J&K in 2019 any Indian citizen may seek information from a J&K UT public authority. No special status, occupation or locus standi is required, and the applicant need give no reason for the request. 'Only journalists and media persons' is wrong — the Act confers no press-specific privilege. 'Only government employees' is wrong — the Act exists to let citizens question the government, not the reverse. 'Only advocates and legal professionals' is wrong — no legal qualification is needed.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The RTI Act does not apply to the state of Jammu and Kashmir (prior to its reorganization in 2019).
Reason (R): J&K had its own separate law called the Jammu and Kashmir Right to Information Act, 2009.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Before 2019 reorganization, the central RTI Act did not apply to J&K (A is correct). J&K had its own RTI Act, 2009 (R is correct and explains why the central Act didn't apply — J&K had special status and its own legislation). Option 2 is wrong because R explains A; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually accurate; Option 4 is wrong because A is also correct. Note: After August 2019 reorganization, the central RTI Act applies to J&K UT.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following sections of the RTI Act, 2005, as applicable to J&K UT public authorities, with their provisions:

Column I:
(a) Section 4
(b) Section 6
(c) Section 8
(d) Section 19

Column II:
(i) Exemptions from disclosure
(ii) Proactive disclosure by public authorities
(iii) Appeal process
(iv) How to request information

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Section 4 imposes the duty of proactive or suo motu disclosure, so (a)-(ii). Section 6 sets out how a citizen makes a request and to whom, so (b)-(iv). Section 8 lists the exemptions a PIO may invoke, so (c)-(i). Section 19 governs first and second appeals, which for J&K public authorities now run to the Central Information Commission at the second stage, so (d)-(iii). The other options variously swap the exemption and appeal provisions or misassign Section 4, and each therefore misplaces at least two pairs.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: After the reorganization of J&K in 2019, the central RTI Act, 2005 is now applicable to:
options: Neither — J&K still has its own RTI Act
Both Jammu & Kashmir UT and Ladakh UT
questions.correctAnswer: Both Jammu & Kashmir UT and Ladakh UT
questions.explanation: After the Jammu & Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019, the central RTI Act, 2005 applies to both new Union Territories. 'Only J&K UT' is wrong — Ladakh is also covered; 'Only Ladakh UT' is wrong — J&K is also covered; 'Neither' is wrong — the central Act now applies to both after abrogation of Article 370.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about filing an RTI application in Jammu & Kashmir:

(i) The application must be in writing or through electronic means.
(ii) The applicant need not give reasons for seeking the information.
(iii) The applicant must furnish proof of Indian citizenship while filing.
(iv) The application may be made in Hindi, English or the official language of the area.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Section 6 requires a written or electronic request. (ii) is correct — an applicant is expressly not obliged to give any reason, only the contact details needed for a reply. (iv) is correct — the request may be in Hindi, English or the official language of the area, which for J&K UT includes Kashmiri, Dogri and Urdu alongside Hindi and English under the J&K Official Languages Act, 2020. (iii) is wrong — no proof of citizenship is demanded at the filing stage, so every option containing (iii) is incorrect.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The committee that recommends the appointment of the Chief Information Commissioner, who heads the Commission now hearing J&K's second appeals, includes which of the following?

(i) The Prime Minister (Chairperson)
(ii) The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha
(iii) A Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister
(iv) The Chief Justice of India

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The selection committee is a three-member body comprising the Prime Minister as chairperson (i), the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha (ii) and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister (iii); the President then appoints on its recommendation. (iv) is wrong — the Chief Justice of India has no role in appointing Information Commissioners, unlike in some other statutory appointments, so every option containing (iv) is incorrect. Since 2019 this Commission is the second-appellate forum for J&K UT public authorities.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The central RTI Act, 2005 replaced the Freedom of Information Act, 2002. The J&K Right to Information Act, 2009 similarly replaced which earlier J&K legislation?
questions.explanation: J&K first legislated on access to information through the J&K Right to Information Act, 2004, which was widely criticised as weak; it was repealed and replaced by the stronger J&K Right to Information Act, 2009, itself repealed in turn by the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019. 'J&K Public Records Act, 1993' is wrong — records legislation governs archiving, not a citizen's right of access. 'J&K Official Secrets Act, 1923' is wrong — secrecy law was the obstacle RTI was designed to overcome. 'J&K Freedom of Information Act, 2002' is wrong — the 2002 Freedom of Information Act was a central enactment, not a J&K one.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: A PIO in Jammu withholds personal information under Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act. Such information may nevertheless be disclosed if:
options: The applicant pays an additional fee of Rs. 500
The information is less than 5 years old
The applicant is a relative of the person concerned
It serves a larger public interest that outweighs the harm to privacy
questions.correctAnswer: It serves a larger public interest that outweighs the harm to privacy
questions.explanation: Section 8(1)(j) shields personal information that has no relationship to any public activity or interest, or that would cause an unwarranted invasion of privacy, but it carries an express override: the information must still be disclosed where the competent authority is satisfied that the larger public interest justifies it. Paying an extra fee is wrong — no amount of money buys an exemption away. The age of the record is wrong — the five-year test appears nowhere in this clause. Being a relative is wrong — the Act is blind to the applicant's identity and relationship.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the number of RTI applications received by a J&K UT department over four years:

2019 → 500
2020 → 320
2021 → 480
2022 → 600

In which year was the percentage increase over the previous year the highest?
questions.explanation: From 320 in 2020 to 480 in 2021 the rise is 160 on a base of 320, that is 50 per cent, the largest year-on-year increase in the series. 2022 is wrong — 480 to 600 is a rise of 120 on 480, only 25 per cent, so although the absolute number is highest that year the percentage growth is half that of 2021. 2020 is wrong — applications actually fell from 500 to 320, a decrease of 36 per cent. 2019 is wrong — no previous year is given, so no increase can be computed for it.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: An applicant in Baramulla wishes to file a second appeal. Which section of the RTI Act deals with the appeal process?
questions.explanation: Section 19 governs appeals, providing for a first appeal to a senior officer within the public authority within 30 days and a second appeal to the Information Commission within 90 days; for J&K UT that second appeal now lies to the Central Information Commission. 'Section 8' is wrong — it lists exemptions from disclosure. 'Section 12' is wrong — it deals with the constitution of the Central Information Commission. 'Section 24' is wrong — it excludes listed intelligence and security organisations from the Act's purview.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the disposal status of RTI applications in a J&K UT government office:

Information provided → 350
Rejected under Section 8 → 80
Transferred to other authority → 45
Pending → 25

What percentage of total applications were rejected?
questions.explanation: The total is 350 + 80 + 45 + 25 = 500 applications, of which 80 were rejected, giving 80/500 = 16 per cent. '18%' is wrong and is what you get by dividing 80 by a mistaken total of about 445, that is by forgetting the pending applications. '20%' is wrong — that would require a total of 400, which ignores both the transferred and the pending categories. '14%' is wrong — it corresponds to no defensible total and understates the rejection rate.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are objectives of extending the RTI Act to Jammu & Kashmir?

(i) To promote transparency in governance
(ii) To reduce corruption in public offices
(iii) To empower citizens to hold the administration accountable
(iv) To classify all government documents as secret

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i), (ii) and (iii) are the Act's declared purposes, recited in its preamble and applied to J&K UT public authorities from 31 October 2019: transparency in governance, containment of corruption, and an empowered citizenry able to hold the administration to account. (iv) is wrong and inverts the statute — the RTI Act was enacted precisely to displace the culture of blanket secrecy associated with the Official Secrets Act, so any option containing (iv) must be rejected.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: Under the RTI Act, as applicable in J&K UT, information over __________ years old, including cabinet papers, shall ordinarily be disclosed on request.
questions.explanation: Section 8(3) provides that, subject to a few named exemptions, information relating to any event or matter that occurred more than 20 years before the request shall be supplied, and this applies to J&K UT public authorities under the central Act. '15 years' is wrong — no such threshold appears in the Act. '25 years' is wrong and overstates the period. '10 years' is wrong and understates it. The rule matters because it opens historical records, including cabinet deliberations, once the twenty-year period has run.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019, which governs the Commission that hears J&K's second appeals:

(i) It allows the Central Government to prescribe the term of office of the Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners.
(ii) It allows the Central Government to determine their salaries and conditions of service.
(iii) Before the amendment, the Chief Information Commissioner's salary was equivalent to that of the Chief Election Commissioner.
(iv) The amendment repealed the RTI Act entirely and replaced it with a new law.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) and (ii) are correct — the 2019 amendment moved both tenure and the salaries and service conditions of the Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners from the statute itself to rules made by the Central Government, a change critics said weakened the Commission's independence. (iii) is correct — the Chief Information Commissioner previously ranked with the Chief Election Commissioner in pay and status. (iv) is wrong — the RTI Act, 2005 remains in force and was merely amended, so every option containing (iv) is incorrect.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following terms with their meanings under the RTI Act, as applied to public authorities in J&K UT:

Column I:
(a) Public Authority
(b) Third Party
(c) Record
(d) Right to Information

Column II:
(i) Includes documents, memos, emails, opinions, press releases and logbooks
(ii) Any authority or body established by the Constitution, by law, or by government notification
(iii) A person other than the citizen making the request, to whom the information relates
(iv) The right of access to information held by public authorities

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: A 'public authority' is any body established or constituted by or under the Constitution, by any law, or by government notification, which after 2019 includes J&K UT departments and bodies, so (a)-(ii). A 'third party' is a person other than the requesting citizen to whom the information relates, so (b)-(iii). A 'record' is defined broadly to take in documents, memos, emails, opinions, press releases and logbooks, so (c)-(i). The 'right to information' is the right of access to information held by public authorities, so (d)-(iv). Every other option misassigns at least two pairs.
